text:
alex: Heads-up — seeing a perf regression on seqlen ~512 workloads after yesterday's kernel-scheduler tweak. p50 up ~22%, p99 spikes intermittently. Appears related to kernel picks choosing GQA path when MQA/paged-kv would be cheaper given current KV layout.

maria: Can you paste the profile or a small reproducer? rough numbers are fine.

alex: Quick excerpt from `nvprof` / runtime traces: 
```
workload: webchat-batched (batch=8 avg_seq=512)
A100 node, paged-kv block_size=64, MQA enabled
kernel_picker: chose gqa_dense_xfer for 39% of requests
latency p50: 48ms (baseline 39ms)
latency p95: 210ms (baseline 160ms)
KV page faults: 112 / min (spike correlated with p95)
L2 utilization: 74% -> thrash during kv loads
```
Trying local tweaks: forcing `mqa_paged_blocksz=128` drops p50 back to ~40ms.

simon: Interesting — sounds like the scoring heuristic missed the seqlen distribution shift. Did the autotuner rebaseline after the scheduler change?

alex: I think autotuner only re-evaluated kernel latency, not layout-induced memory overhead. The score is basically latency + alpha * mem_pressure. alpha is too small for paged-kv.

katie: Can you show the kernel-scoring config? maybe add seqlen-hist gating so for >384 we bias toward mqa_paged path.

alex: current snippet: 
```yaml
kernel_score: 
  latency_weight: 0.85
  mem_weight: 0.15
  seqlen_bias: 0.0
  prefetch_hint: auto
```
We should probably add `seqlen_bias` and a `kv_page_frag_penalty` tuned per block_size.

raj: TLDR: small block_size (64) + GQA kernel => more scattered KV reads -> L2 misses -> stalls. Increasing block_size reduces fragmentation and aggregates loads. But that may increase cold-start memory. we need a dynamic choice.

andrew: Could we add a cheap online probe: maintain a rolling seqlen histogram per route and switch kernel scoring function when >50% of requests are in [384,1024]? cheap to compute.

simon: yep. Implement gating: if hist_frac(>384) > 0.5 then set `seqlen_bias = +0.2` and `mem_weight = 0.3` for a minute, re-evaluate. Also add a hystersis to avoid flip-flopping.

katie: I'll run the reproducer with block_size=128 and collect differences. measurements: batch=8,30min run. I'll paste numbers in a bit.

perf-bot: nightly-regression check: https://ci.redwood.ai/perf/2024/17788-gqa-mqa-kvpage (summary: +18% p50 on route webchat-batched) :eyes:

alex: thanks — action items: 1) simon add seqlen-hist gating + hysteresis to kernel_picker, 2) katie run block_size=128 reproducer and attach logs, 3) raj draft a kv_page_frag_penalty heuristic (function of block_size, avg_seqlen, kv_hits), 4) perf run to validate on canary.

maria: +1. Also add a short unit test that simulates high fragmentation and ensures kernel_picker prefers mqa_paged when mem_penalty > threshold.

andrew: I'll add a small dashboard card: per-route seqlen distribution + kernel path fraction + KV page faults so SRE can watch during rollouts.

alex: I'll open a PR with profile and small patch to score function, pinging you all. pinging @simon @katie for triage. :thumbsup:
